message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

**What I did and why:** I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and checked the live quote (last $420.18, bid $420.16 / ask $420.20 as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC). The filing shows a strong, broad-based year: **total revenue of $245,122 million (fiscal 2024)**, up 16% from $211,915 million, with operating income of $109,433 million (+24%), net income of $88,136 million (+22%), and diluted EPS of $11.80; Microsoft Cloud revenue grew 23% to $137.4 billion and operating cash flow rose to $118.5 billion. Growth was driven by Intelligent Cloud (revenue $105,362 million, +20%, with Azure and other cloud services up 30%) and Productivity and Business Processes ($77,728 million, +12%), with the Activision Blizzard acquisition ($75.4 billion, closed October 2023) adding scale in Gaming. The balance sheet remains very strong ($75.5 billion cash and short-term investments, AAA-rated long-term debt), and the main watch items are heavy AI/datacenter capex ($44.5 billion additions to property and equipment) and the IRS's proposed $28.9 billion transfer-pricing adjustment, which management is contesting. On that basis I placed a single buy order within your mandate: **23 shares of MSFT at a limit of $421.00** (about 0.2% above the last trade, i.e., close to market), which filled at $421.00 for roughly **$9,683** — under the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, with no cash withdrawn from the account (cash was $50,000 and you already held 100 MSFT shares). The key figures cited on the order are fiscal 2024 revenue of $245,122 million, operating income of $109,433 million, and net income of $88,136 million.
